context.canonical_title: JVM OOM 如何定位和处理？

required_checks: Verify heap, Metaspace, native/thread and container OOM boundaries against current primary Oracle/OpenJDK documentation.
Verify HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError scope and HeapDumpPath behavior; do not imply heap dumps exist for every resource exhaustion mode.
Verify jcmd command impact, NMT startup requirement, NMT baseline/diff semantics and NMT non-JVM-allocation coverage limits.
Verify JFR/GC/heap/native evidence workflow, capacity reasoning, restart/idempotency boundary, sensitive diagnostic artifact handling and rollout validation.
Verify every source question/variant is directly covered and the scenario answer contains assumptions, diagnosis, mitigation, observability, validation and trade-offs.
Reject any wording that implies fabricated personal incident experience or unsupported numeric production facts.
review_contract.promotion_boundary: Do not promote or fabricate human approval. Pilot human review remains a separate mandatory gate when required by config.

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: Oracle JDK 25 Troubleshoot Memory Leaks
claims_to_check: OutOfMemoryError has multiple causes including Java heap, native memory and GC overhead conditions
heap dumps and JFR can support memory-leak diagnosis
JFR must be running when the leak occurs and is designed for low-overhead production use

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: Oracle JDK 25 java Command
claims_to_check: HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError and HeapDumpPath behavior and scope
diagnostic tools should match the target JDK version where required

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: Oracle JDK 25 jcmd Command
claims_to_check: GC.class_histogram and GC.heap_dump are high-impact operations
VM.native_memory exposes summary/detail/baseline and diff operations
VM.metaspace and thread diagnostics are available with documented impact

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: Oracle JDK 25 Diagnostic Tools and Native Memory Tracking
claims_to_check: NMT tracks HotSpot VM internal native memory and does not track non-JVM code allocations
NMT can be used with baseline and later comparisons to investigate growth
